studies.Population: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition participants
studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Red meat, dietary nitrosamines, and heme iron and risk of bladder cancer in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC).
studies.Authors: Jakszyn P, González CA, Luján-Barroso L, Ros MM, Bueno-de-Mesquita HB, Roswall N, Tjønneland AM, Büchner FL, Egevad L, Overvad K, Raaschou-Nielsen O, Clavel-Chapelon F, Boutron-Ruault MC, Touillaud MS, Chang-Claude J, Allen NE, Kiemeney LA, Key TJ, Kaaks R, Boeing H, Weikert S, Trichopoulou A, Oikonomou E, Zylis D, Palli D, Berrino F, Vineis P, Tumino R, Mattiello A, Peeters PH, Parr CL, Gram IT, Skeie G, Sánchez MJ, Larrañaga N, Ardanaz E, Navarro C, Rodríguez L, Ulmert D, Ehrnström R, Hallmans G, Ljungberg B, Roddam AW, Bingham SA, Khaw KT, Slimani N, Boffetta PA, Jenab M, Mouw T, Michaud DS, Riboli E
studies.Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
studies.comparison_type: Per doubling of heme iron intake

sample_size.excerpt: Data on food consumption and complete follow-up for cancer occurrence were available for a total of 481,419 participants, recruited in 10 European countries.

cases.excerpt: After a mean follow-up of 8.7 years, 1,001 participants were diagnosed with bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: We found no overall association between intake of red meat (log2 HR: 1.06; 95% CI: 0.99-1.13), nitrosamines (log2 HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.92-1.30 and HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.92-1.05 for ENOC and NDMA, respectively) or heme iron (log2 HR: 1.05; 95 CI: 0.99-1.12) and bladder cancer risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: We found no overall association between intake of red meat (log2 HR: 1.06; 95% CI: 0.99-1.13), nitrosamines (log2 HR: 1.09; 95% CI: 0.92-1.30 and HR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.92-1.05 for ENOC and NDMA, respectively) or heme iron (log2 HR: 1.05; 95 CI: 0.99-1.12) and bladder cancer risk.

design.excerpt: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)

timing.excerpt: After a mean follow-up of 8.7 years

gender.excerpt: stratified by age at recruitment, gender, and study center

smoking_status.excerpt: The associations did not vary by sex, high- versus low-risk bladder cancers, smoking status, or occupation
